title: Check-ruling: a freeze refusal line may open with the command's name
situation: The meaning-roles freeze checks (workflow 24-38, held-out workflow 1-2 where they share the helper) require a refusal's one line to begin with 'concepts <verb>:'. The command prints every capability refusal as '<command> <message>', so the line reads 'cratylus concepts supersede: …'. The examples fix that the change is refused before anything is appended, not the form of the line; the lead's contract wording ('one line, concepts <verb>: …') was read as the line's start. The checks are frozen; changing them is the architect's check-ruling.
decision: Rule the freeze checks' refusal-form assertion to accept the command's name before 'concepts <verb>:', the rest of the check unchanged; the command's refusal convention stays.
consequences: Until ruled, the journal-refusal assertion of the freeze checks fails on the line's form alone; the lead reports which examples fail only for that reason.
